analysis:
Examined all supplied patches, BASE/HEAD source and mode metadata against the canonical index and selected definitions. No independently supported regression was established. ci-master.yml HEAD 80–143 and 230–290 conditionally disable cache restore/save and add checks rejecting cached Git symlinks, hooks and selected executable/include configuration before Git validation. This strengthens existing cache handling, but does not establish that arbitrary cached Git configuration is inert; cache trust and poisoning exposure require integration verification. Push-only saves, read-only permissions and credential-free Git caching remain unchanged.
Desktop HEAD 31, 61–95 newly routes manual unsigned packaging through darkbloom-route.yml, retains disabled signing discovery and review-only artifacts, and adds a timeout. Desktop 41–55, 69–83 and landing HEAD 38–51 disable npm caching on named Sandbox runners without a cache URL. These guards do not themselves implement endpoint redirection or authenticate a cache service. Integration should verify runner-name/environment provenance, cache isolation and redirection, and whether logged DARKBLOOM_CACHE_URL values are credential-free.
Provider-plan.yml patch HEAD 174–185 lowers runtime lane sizes, removes required-shape markers from build/check lanes and adds GPU lanes. Reconcile with provider-tests.yml and routing evidence: confirm new build runners' isolation/artifact trust, GPU lane consumption, and revised tests' peak memory rather than treating BASE memory comments as proof of current exhaustion. Relevant artifact/qualification assets are A-011/A-017 and T-054; runtime confidentiality, authorization, billing and T-041 inference-cache controls are not directly changed here. Missing routing and test implementations leave material new-runner trust and availability questions for integration, not evidence of a vulnerability.
